title: The Rough Monsoon
premise: Vesper Pemberton, a desert ranger who has spent a decade outrunning the grief of a drowned expedition, tracks a thief across the salt flats only to discover the stolen map leads to the Marlowe wreck — the ship her father died salvaging, and the one job her crew swore off forever. When old rival Cassian Vane hires them with six tides before his salvage fleet reaches it, Vesper must choose between the identity she built as a drifter and the inheritance she buried. Racing storms, saboteurs, and her own crew's fractured loyalties, she reaches the wreck at the final tide and finds not treasure but her father's log — proof he chose the crew over the fortune. In the end, Vesper claims neither gold nor vengeance: she sinks the wreck's location beneath the monsoon and finally stops running, going home.
about_author: Marguerite Voss is the pen name of a former maritime surveyor who spent seven years charting coastlines from Oman to Zanzibar before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people who mistake distance for freedom.

chapters.title: Salt on the Wind
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She tracks a thief named Idris across the salt flats for nine days, refusing to stop even when her water runs low, because stopping means thinking. The emotional beat is restless avoidance — she'd rather chase than arrive.

chapters.title: The Thief Who Waited
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She corners Idris in a canyon ruin, but he didn't run to escape; he ran so she would find him. He carries half a chart to the Marlowe wreck. The beat is uneasy recognition: someone has been hunting her deliberately.

chapters.title: An Old Debt Wearing New Clothes
chapters.summary: Cassian Vane's POV. The rival who once left Vesper's father's expedition to die offers her crew a contract: reach the Marlowe before his own salvage fleet, in six tides. The beat is poisoned temptation wrapped in charm.

chapters.title: Crew of the Long Way Around
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Back at port, she faces her crew — engineer Sefa, navigator Bram, deckhand Orla — each of whom lost someone on the Marlowe. The sworn-off job splits them. The beat is grief surfacing after years underwater.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Against her own judgment, she signs. Sefa joins out of loyalty, Bram refuses and stays ashore, Orla follows for reasons she won't name. The beat is the terrible relief of choosing motion over stillness.

chapters.title: Departure in Gray Water
chapters.summary: Orla's POV. They slip past harbor officials and Vane's watchers aboard the patched ketch Kestrel. Orla reveals she was a child survivor of the Marlowe's last voyage. The beat is fragile trust forming between damaged people.

chapters.title: The Chart That Lies
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Decoding Idris's half-chart, they realize it's incomplete by design — Vane gave them only enough to lead his fleet if they fail. Someone aboard may be feeding him their position. The beat is creeping paranoia.

chapters.title: First Tide: The Drowned Coast
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. They navigate the reef graveyard where her father's expedition scattered. Vesper relives the night she swam away and he didn't surface. The beat is memory as undertow.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The Kestrel's rudder is fouled overnight; they lose a tide repairing it in shark waters. Evidence points to Bram, who secretly followed them. The beat is betrayal sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Second Tide: The Stowaway
chapters.summary: Orla's POV. They catch Bram hiding in the hold — he came not to stop them but because the Marlowe took his brother, and he needs to see it. Vesper must decide whether mercy costs them the race. The beat is anger giving way to shared mourning.

chapters.title: Vane's Fleet on the Horizon
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Smoke on the horizon: Vane's fleet has cut ahead through the strait. A storm front builds behind them all. The beat is dread — the race has become a three-way collision with weather.

chapters.title: Third Tide: Running Before the Storm
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. A brutal passage through the squall line; the Kestrel nearly founders, and Orla saves the rigging at the cost of a broken arm. The beat is the crew becoming a single organism under pressure.

chapters.title: What Vane Wants
chapters.summary: Cassian Vane's POV. Aboard his flagship, we learn Vane isn't after treasure — the Marlowe carried sealed ledgers proving he sold out the original expedition, and he must destroy them. The beat is villainy revealed as fear.

chapters.title: Fourth Tide: The Liar's Channel
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The half-chart leads through a channel that doesn't exist on any modern survey — her father's secret route. Following it feels like hearing his voice again. The beat is inheritance as both gift and trap.

chapters.title: Fifth Tide: The Wreck
chapters.summary: Orla's POV. They find the Marlowe upright in a deep lagoon, eerily preserved. Divers descend; Vesper enters the cabin where her father died. The beat is awe curdling into horror as Vane's fleet rounds the headland.

chapters.title: The Logbook
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. In the captain's safe: her father's log. It records that he scuttled the salvage payout to save his drowning crew — including young Vesper — choosing lives over the fortune, and naming Vane's betrayal. The beat is devastating redefinition of everything she ran from.

chapters.title: Boarders
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Vane's men storm the lagoon at slack water. The crew fights to hold the Kestrel and the log while the monsoon breaks fully overhead. The beat is desperate, close-quarters courage.

chapters.title: Sixth Tide
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Climax. With the fleet closing, Vesper confronts Vane on the pitching decks, log in hand, and offers him the choice her father made: the treasure or the truth. His greed dooms his flagship on the reef. The beat is fury transmuted into clarity.

chapters.title: What the Sea Keeps
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. In the storm's aftermath, the crew votes — not to sell the log or the location, but to let the sea keep its dead. Vane survives, stripped of fleet and reputation. The beat is collective release.

chapters.title: The Weight of Stopping
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Ashore, Vesper faces the stillness she has fled for a decade: no contract, no chase, her father's log closed. Grief arrives honestly for the first time. The beat is the terror and necessity of standing still.

chapters.title: Home Water
chapters.summary: Orla's POV. The crew, now family, refits the Kestrel not for salvage but for survey work — mapping coasts so others come home alive. Orla finally speaks her full account of the sinking. The beat is belonging chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: Monsoon Season
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Epilogue. Rain falls clean over the harbor; Vesper plants her father's compass on the cliff above the drowned coast and stays. She is no longer a ranger tracking nothing — she is a keeper of what remains. The beat is quiet, earned peace.
